 AI Summary 
 XRP fell below $0.90 this week, setting a lower low, but its weekly relative strength index held above the June trough, leaving room for a rebound. The market is watching whether XRP can close the week back above $1. XRP traded near $0.9601 on Nov. 17. RSI rose to 35.23 despite a lower price, though it remains well below 50.

 XRP dipped below $0.90 this week, setting a lower low, but its weekly relative strength index (RSI) stayed above the June trough, leaving open the possibility of a rebound.
 On Nov. 17, The Crypto Basic, a blockchain media outlet, reported that the market is focusing on whether XRP can reclaim $1 in its weekly close.
 XRP traded around $0.9601 as of Nov. 17, about 4.2 percent below $1. Earlier, XRP slid to $0.8943 on Nov. 14 before recouping part of the decline, and the next day it formed a weekly close around $0.975. It has still not regained $1.
 This bullish divergence formed by comparing two downswings. In June, XRP was above $1, but its 14-week RSI fell below 30, a level commonly viewed as the oversold threshold. In November, the price fell further, but the RSI posted 35.23.
 Still, an improved RSI alone does not confirm a rebound. An RSI of 35.23 remains far below the benchmark of 50, leaving room for a broader bearish trend even if downside pressure eases.
 The first confirmation signal for a rebound is whether the weekly close rises above $1 again. Even if a pullback follows, XRP would need to hold $1 for support to form above the November low and for the $1.10 area to come back into view. XRP ended its weekly close around $1.11 on Nov. 8, but fell back below $1 just a week later.
 On the downside, support levels are also clear. The $0.89 to $0.90 zone overlaps with around $0.90, the lower band of the daily Bollinger Bands. If the weekly close forms below the November low, the likelihood of a reversal weakens and the long-term support zone in the $0.78 range could draw renewed attention.
 Ultimately, XRP's direction will not be decided by technical bullish signals alone. Whether the price can regain $1 and settle above it on a weekly closing basis is the first confirmation zone for a rebound, and if it fails, whether it can defend the $0.90 level is expected to become the market's key variable again.
